throughput_requirements: Customer asks for deterministic, reserved throughput guarantees. Current working numbers: 120k tokens/sec sustained aggregate (target), with concurrency cap ~800 active sessions. Per-node planning: assume 12 reserved GPUs with 10k sustained tokens/sec per GPU on their workload mix. Burst policy: allow ephemeral bursts up to 200k tokens/sec for up to 60 seconds during flash sales, with automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if sustained >90s. Require per-tenant token throttles, priority queues for critical traffic, and soft preemption. Also requests clear credit for partial burst exhaustion and credits refill policy.
latency_slos: Primary SLO: 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms for chat workloads at target concurrency. Secondary: 99th percentile <= 300ms for customer-facing routing tier. Wants explicit ramp behavior (how SLOs degrade with load) and a clause for penalty/credits if sustained violation >3 consecutive hours.
reserved_gpu_planning_notes: Discussed two sizing options: (A) 12xH100-class reserved (higher perf, lower latency margin) vs (B) 18xA100-class (cost efficient, higher aggregate concurrency). Customer leans to H100s for latency-sensitive reranking paths and A100 for background batch embedding jobs. Need conversion guidance: tokens/sec -> GPU allocation table; Redwood to provide model-specific perf curves for gpt-like family + quantized variants.
sla_negotiation_points: Must-haves: uptime SLA 99.95% for dedicated capacity, clear incident definitions, scheduled maintenance windows, penalty/credit formula tied to user-visible latency SLOs and throughput guarantees. Wants explicit fallback routing to hosted model pool with defined cost uplift and data handling during fallback. Legal requests data residency appendix for EU customers and stronger audit log retention (1 year).
